title: C-6 — Run manifest
description:
One JSON per run, written by the launcher BEFORE the run and finalised after. F-20: every experiment reproducible from a single config file plus a seed.

`vehicle` is 'hardware' or 'simulator', and F-24 requires every simulated figure to be labelled. Make the figure scripts READ THIS FIELD and stamp the plot automatically — labelling by hand fails exactly once, in the final report.

vehicle.description: F-24: figure scripts read this and stamp simulated plots automatically.

trace_sha256.description: The trace's identity everywhere downstream. Replay client verifies before t0.

warmup_s.description: Drives is_warmup in C-5, computed from the trace's intended_offset_s in BOTH vehicles.

cost_model_snapshots.description: node_id -> C-3 snapshot_id. Which snapshot each node's estimate came from.

items.description:
Everything runtime-specific — ignore_eos, min_tokens/max_tokens, slot reuse disabled — is set once at engine construction and recorded HERE, so the settings that eliminate your confounds are auditable from the results.

F-9: every POOL node runs the same engine (llama.cpp + GGUF). Engine and quantization are held constant so that the heterogeneity ratio R is a property of hardware and node configuration ALONE. What varies per node is engine_config (F-9a). A node with role='engine_gap_probe' is the F-9b measured condition and is NOT a pool member: it participates in no policy comparison.

engine.description: F-9: 'llamacpp' for every pool member. 'vllm' is legal ONLY on a node with role='engine_gap_probe' (F-9b).

quant.description: GGUF quantization for pool nodes, e.g. 'Q4_K_M'. Held constant across the pool (F-9).

gpu.description: 'none' for CPU-only nodes. The pool spans GPU and CPU machines running the SAME engine.

role.description: F-9b: the engine-gap probe is a measured condition, not a pool member. It appears in no figure other than the engine-gap result, and the pipeline MUST exclude it from every policy comparison.

engine_config.description: F-9a: per-node capability, expressed as runtime parameters of the single engine. THIS IS WHAT SETS R. Because R is now synthesized from configuration rather than from engine differences, these values are part of the experimental condition and must be recorded per run, not merely per machine.

parallel.description: llama.cpp --parallel: the fixed slot count. This is exactly SimNode.batch_capacity in the DES — the simulator's node model is now exact rather than approximate.

clock_sync.description:
How far apart the pool's clocks were, measured at LAN setup and recorded here.

Optional, and absent means exactly that: not measured. It is NOT a claim that the offset was zero.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CORRECT. There is still no cross-host subtraction anywhere in C-4 or C-5, so `offset_ms` corrects nothing: every duration is single-host, and `transport_residual_ms` is a difference of such durations in which a constant offset cancels. It is recorded as evidence that the clocks were being disciplined, so the claim can be checked rather than taken. The offset also could not help with the two on-wire timestamps (`client_send_mono_ns`, `worker_mono_ns`) even in principle, because those are CLOCK_MONOTONIC reads whose zero is each machine's boot; an NTP offset says nothing about the gap between two boot times. That is why F-18's transport decomposition stays out of reach regardless.

`rate_error_ppm` is the field that touches a number. A worker clock ticking r ppm faster than the reference inflates worker-local durations by r ppm relative to client-local ones, and that is multiplicative, so it does not cancel. The pipeline divides it out and reports the size of the correction.

reference.description: Host whose timebase corrected durations are expressed in. The client host, because e2e_ms is what everything else is reconciled against.

max_abs_offset_ms.description: Largest offset between any two hosts, not between a host and its upstream source.

max_rate_error_ppm.description: Largest rate difference between any two hosts. The term the pipeline divides out.

hosts.description: host -> that machine's clock as its own time daemon described it.

method.description: 'declared' means a human wrote the number in; it is kept distinguishable from a machine reading on purpose.

synchronised.description: False means the daemon was running but tracking nothing. Its other numbers are stale and are not recorded.

offset_ms.description: Positive when this host reads ahead of its reference.

dispersion_ms.description: The daemon's own bound on the offset.

rate_error_ppm.description: Signed residual frequency error left after discipline.

skew_ppm.description: The daemon's own bound on rate_error_ppm.

transport_overhead.description:
What a client observes on top of the engine's own span in this environment: the gRPC hop in, the decision, the dispatch to the worker, and the F-11 direct return.

Optional, and absent means not measured. It is NOT a claim that the overhead was zero, and a consumer that finds it absent applies nothing rather than guessing a default.

It is a summary of C-5 `transport_residual_ms` over the warmed-up, status-ok rows of runs on this environment, so it inherits that field's honesty: a residual of single-host durations, never a cross-host subtraction. Pooling across operating points is the right shape because the quantity is a property of the wiring rather than of the load; on the 1B anchors it moves from 5.37 ms at quiet to 5.63 ms at heavy while service time moves by a factor of ten.

WHY IT IS IN MILLISECONDS AND NOT A FRACTION. A simulator that reproduces service time from C-3 alone is short by exactly this, and the temptation is to close the gap with a percentage. A percentage would charge a 13-second request 650 ms of network where a 1-second request pays 50 ms, which is the opposite of what the wire does. The term is additive because the thing it models is additive.

sd_ms.description: Population standard deviation over the same rows.

source.description: How it was measured, in words, so the number can be argued with.

measured_from.description: run_ids the summary was pooled over.

f18_status.description: 'partial' when the pinned engine version does not expose the prefill/decode split. Record it here rather than faking the split.

send_lag_violations.description: Non-zero => run marked invalid and NOT analysed.

colocated_nodes.description: F-9a: throttling MUST be applied to distinct physical machines. Co-located logical nodes contend for PCIe, memory bandwidth and cache, which would reintroduce as contention the confound F-9 (single engine) removes. Count of nodes sharing a `host` with another node. MUST be 0 for a valid run.

clock_unsynced_hosts.description: Hosts in `clock_sync.hosts` whose time daemon reported no discipline. Optional, and absent means the run predates the field or had no clock block at all.\n\nReported, never fatal. The pipeline acts only on the rate error, since a constant offset cancels in a difference of single-host durations, and 100 ppm on a 900 ms request is 0.09 ms. An unsynchronised host costs the evidence that the durations were comparable, not the durations themselves.
